name: Leaning Tower of Pisa
overview: The Leaning Tower of Pisa is the freestanding bell tower of the cathedral in Pisa, Italy. Famous worldwide for its unintended tilt, it's one of the most recognizable architectural structures in the world.
history: This 'beautiful mistake' began leaning during construction in 1173 when the foundation settled unevenly into soft clay soil. Legend says Galileo Galilei dropped cannonballs from the top in 1589 to prove his theory of gravity - that all objects fall at the same rate regardless of mass, revolutionizing physics forever. The tower's tilt increased for centuries, reaching a dangerous 5.5 degrees by 1990. Engineers feared it would collapse, so they stabilized it between 1990-2001 using counterweights, cables, and soil extraction. Today, at a safe 3.97 degrees, it's actually more stable than it has been in 600 years! The tower is part of the 'Field of Miracles' (Campo dei Miracoli), a stunning complex of white marble buildings that showcases Pisa's medieval wealth as a powerful maritime republic rivaling Venice and Genoa.
highlights: Iconic lean of 3.97 degrees from vertical
294 steps spiral staircase to the top
Beautiful Romanesque architecture with blind arcades
Part of the stunning Piazza dei Miracoli (Square of Miracles)
tips: Book climbing tickets in advance - limited to 30 people every 30 minutes. Wear comfortable shoes for the spiral stairs. Don't forget the classic 'pushing the tower' photo opportunity!
